newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end higher, Reliance leads the way.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end higher, Reliance leads the way.

text.p: Indian shares ended higher on Tuesday with petrochemicals giant Reliance Industries leading the uptrend ahead of a crucial board meeting later this week, traders said.
Reliance is due to announce a bonus issue of shares at a board meeting on Thursday. The firm will also hold its annual shareholders meeting on that day.
"The stock is likely to go up further before the bonus issue is announced," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
Reliance shares ended 7.50 rupees, or nearly two percent, higher at 374.50 -- a touch off the day's high of 374.75.

Reliance shares surged 13 percent last week. Traders expect the company to announce a bonus ratio of three shares for every five shares held -- the same ratio the firm gave investors in its last two bonus issues.
Traders said foreign funds continued to be buyers in stocks like tractor maker Mahindra & Mahindra, scooter maker Bajaj Auto, oil firm ONGC and pharmaceuticals firm Glaxo.
EIH Ltd -- the flagship of the Oberoi group of hotels -- said its net profit climbed to 1.38 billion rupees in the year ended March 31, from 1.20 billion in the previous year.
The results were slightly below market consensus.
Results from hospitality firm Indian Hotels are also expected later in the day.
Shares of truckmaker TELCO and tobacco conglomerate ITC were battered minutes before close on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on the last day of the weekly settlement, traders said.
TELCO shares fell to a low of 430 -- sharply off the day's high of 465 rupees -- before rallying to end at 445.
ITC crashed to 463 rupees but bounced back to end 0.25 rupees lower at 495. It had hit a day's high of 505 rupees.
"A lot of speculators squared off their positions on the last day of the NSE account, another trader said.
The NSE index ended 1.60 points higher at 1155.30.
In Delhi, the index closed 1.81 points higher at 867.30.
